canonical_statement: Let (X_n) be independent real-valued random variables on a probability space and let c > 0. Put Y_n = X_n on {|X_n| <= c} and Y_n = 0 otherwise. Then the series sum X_n converges almost surely if and only if: sum P(|X_n| > c) is finite, the numerical series sum E[Y_n] converges, and sum Var(Y_n) is finite.

hypotheses: the family X is mutually independent
conclusion: Almost-sure convergence of sum_n X_n is equivalent to the tail-probability, truncated-expectation, and truncated-variance series conditions.
